EKOREST vs Go Ho: Best 4th of July Porch Goose Outfit (2026)

EKOREST ($14.99) vs Go Ho ($15.99) — dressing your porch goose for Independence Day is a beloved American tradition. These two patriotic costumes compete for the best fit, quality, and curb appeal.

Published November 6, 2026 · Based on verified Amazon product data and real customer outcomes

Porch geese have been a quirky staple of American front-yard decor since the 1980s, and dressing them up for holidays has become a full-blown subculture. For the 4th of July, nothing beats a patriotic goose outfit — stars, stripes, and all the red-white-and-blue your lawn statue can handle. Two of the most popular options for standard 23-inch geese are the EKOREST 4th of July Porch Goose Outfit and the Go Ho Patriotic Porch Goose Clothes. Both promise to turn your concrete bird into a star-spangled showstopper. But which one actually delivers?

Quick Verdict

Buy the EKOREST if: You want a complete outfit that's thoughtfully designed — it includes a dress, hat, and cape with clear American flag imagery. The fabric is durable polyester that holds up through rain and sun, and the fit on standard 23-inch geese is spot-on.

Buy the Go Ho if: You prefer a slightly dressier look with the lace bonnet style and want the included flag accessory. The fabric quality is comparable, but the fit runs slightly looser on some statues.

Our pick: The EKOREST 4th of July Porch Goose Outfit. At $14.99, it's the better value with a more secure fit, weather-resistant fabric, and a design that looks great from the curb. The complete three-piece set (dress, hat, and cape) gives you everything you need in one package.

Our Pick 🏆 EKOREST 4th of July Porch Goose Outfit

$14.99 on Amazon

The EKOREST 4th of July Porch Goose Outfit is designed specifically for standard 23-inch lawn goose statues — the most common size you'll find at garden centers and online. The set includes a patriotic dress featuring red and white stripes with a blue bodice covered in white stars, a matching star-spangled hat, and an American flag cape that drapes over the goose's back. It's a complete ensemble that makes your porch goose the talk of the neighborhood.

The fabric is 100% polyester with a tight weave that resists fading from sun exposure and doesn't get waterlogged in summer rain showers. The seams are double-stitched along stress points — particularly around the neck opening and armholes — so you're not dealing with unraveling threads after the first use. The dress closes with Velcro along the back, which makes it easy to put on and take off without wrestling with your statue.

One detail that sets the EKOREST apart is the fabric weight. It's substantial enough to drape nicely without looking stiff, but not so heavy that it slides off the goose in a breeze. The hat stays put with an elastic band underneath, and the cape attaches with a simple hook-and-loop closure at the neck. For the 250th USA anniversary celebrations, EKOREST added an embroidered "1776" detail on the cape lining — a nice touch that shows they put thought into this beyond just printing stars on fabric.

Key specs: 100% polyester, 3-piece set (dress + hat + cape), fits 23-inch statues, Velcro back closure, elastic hat band, machine washable, USA flag design with embroidered details.

Go Ho 4th of July Patriotic Porch Goose Outfit

$15.99 on Amazon

The Go Ho 4th of July Porch Goose Outfit offers a dressier take on patriotic goose fashion. The design features a red, white, and blue dress with a lace-trimmed bonnet instead of a structured hat, giving it a more vintage Americana look. It also includes a small handheld American flag accessory that tucks into a side pocket on the dress — a charming touch that adds personality.

The fabric is a polyester-cotton blend that feels softer to the touch than the EKOREST's all-polyester construction. That softness comes with a trade-off: the fabric is slightly less weather-resistant. In humid conditions, the cotton content can absorb moisture and sag, and the colors may fade faster with prolonged sun exposure compared to all-polyester alternatives. The dress also uses Velcro closure in the back, but the strip is narrower — about half the width of the EKOREST's closure — which can make it trickier to align on bulkier statues.

The Go Ho's standout feature is the lace bonnet. It's genuinely cute, with delicate scalloped edges and a ribbon tie under the chin. But that ribbon is the weak point: it's a single thin strip of satin that can come untied in wind, and several reviewers note it frayed after one season. The included flag accessory is a fun addition, though the flag itself is printed on thin felt rather than fabric, so it curls and fades quickly outdoors.

Key specs: Polyester-cotton blend, 3-piece set (dress + lace bonnet + flag accessory), fits 23-inch statues, narrow Velcro closure, ribbon-tie bonnet, hand wash recommended.

Fit & Sizing

Both outfits are designed for 23-inch lawn geese — the industry standard size. The EKOREST dress has a more structured silhouette with defined "armholes" (wing holes, really) that keep the outfit sitting properly on the statue. The Velcro closure runs the full length of the back, giving you about 3 inches of adjustability. The Go Ho dress is cut more loosely, which means it can accommodate slightly larger statues but may hang awkwardly on smaller ones. If your goose is exactly 23 inches, the EKOREST fits like it was tailored. If your goose is closer to 25 inches, the Go Ho's looser cut might actually work better.

Design & Curb Appeal

From 20 feet away — which is how most neighbors will see your goose — the EKOREST reads clearly as a patriotic outfit. The bold stripes and star field are high-contrast and visible from the street. The Go Ho's bonnet gives it a sweeter, more old-fashioned look, but the lighter pastel tones in the dress don't pop as much at a distance. Up close, the EKOREST's embroidered details (the "1776" on the cape, the stitched stars on the bodice) give it a premium feel that the Go Ho's printed-on designs lack.

Durability & Weather Resistance

This is the category where the EKOREST pulls ahead decisively. The all-polyester construction shrugs off rain — water beads and rolls off rather than soaking in. The colors are dye-sublimated, meaning they're bonded into the fibers rather than printed on the surface, so they resist fading even through a full summer of direct sun. The Go Ho's cotton-blend fabric absorbs moisture more readily, which can lead to mildew if you forget to bring it inside after a rainy night. The printed star pattern on the Go Ho dress also shows wear faster, with edges blurring after a season of use.

Which Should You Buy?

If you want a porch goose outfit that looks great, fits properly, and survives a full summer of sun and the occasional thunderstorm, the EKOREST 4th of July Porch Goose Outfit is the clear choice. At $14.99, it's actually a dollar less than the Go Ho while delivering better fabric, better construction, and better weather resistance. The embroidered details are the kind of thing your neighbors will notice when they walk up your driveway.

The Go Ho is a solid alternative if you specifically want the lace bonnet look or have a slightly oversized goose statue that needs the looser fit. But for most people — and most geese — the EKOREST is the better buy. It's one of those rare cases where the cheaper product is also the better product.

🇺🇸 Pro Tip: To keep your porch goose outfit looking fresh all summer, spray it lightly with Scotchgard fabric protector before putting it outside. Store it indoors (not in a damp garage) between holidays. For the Go Ho's bonnet, replace the satin ribbon with a strip of Velcro or a stronger grosgrain ribbon — it'll last seasons instead of weeks.
